project.researchNotes: Catalogue-addition settlement gate. Nearby attractions and heritage properties do not inflate the settlement score. Score corrected after removal of the artificial sub-60 catalogue gate. Settlement merit was assessed before applying the map threshold; standalone attractions were not transferred into the town score.

touristAppeal.label: Focused Interest
touristAppeal.summary: A focused literary and medieval-church stop with a seasonal community café and rare house-opening days, but too little independent settlement depth for the main town map.
touristAppeal.dogAccessSummary: The wider rural setting supports responsible outdoor walking, but indoor policies are unconfirmed and Arbuthnott House and Gardens explicitly exclude dogs.

visitorHighlights.name: The Grassic Gibbon Centre
visitorHighlights.reason: Arbuthnott’s clearest public draw and a nationally relevant literary collection, though seasonal and specialist rather than a broad museum.
visitorHighlights.openingTimes: Seasonal April–October; telephone ahead for current daily hours
visitorHighlights.admission: Café and shop free to enter; exhibition charge may apply

editorialReview.scoreRationale: Arbuthnott’s clearest public draw and a nationally relevant literary collection, though seasonal and specialist rather than a broad museum.

visitorHighlights.name: St Ternan’s Church and Grassic Gibbon Memorial
visitorHighlights.reason: An unusually complete and accessible medieval church with strong literary connections, but a compact and quiet visit.
visitorHighlights.openingTimes: Open daily; worship may restrict sightseeing

editorialReview.scoreRationale: An unusually complete and accessible medieval church with strong literary connections, but a compact and quiet visit.

visitorHighlights.name: Arbuthnott House and Gardens
visitorHighlights.reason: A distinctive private historic house and early garden, materially limited by a small set of pre-booked house days and seasonal garden access.
visitorHighlights.tagline: Rarely opened family seat and garden
visitorHighlights.openingTimes: House on listed 2026 dates by advance booking; gardens May–July 10:00–16:00 by advance notice

editorialReview.scoreRationale: A distinctive private historic house and early garden, materially limited by a small set of pre-booked house days and seasonal garden access.

townGuide.characterTag: Sunset Song country and medieval St Ternan’s
townGuide.headline: A worthwhile specialist stop, not a complete visitor town
townGuide.intro: Arbuthnott is rewarding for Lewis Grassic Gibbon readers and medieval-church enthusiasts. The centre, café and church form a coherent short visit; the house and garden add interest only on limited advertised days.
bestFor: Lewis Grassic Gibbon and Sunset Song
perfectFor: A literary detour through the Mearns

suggestedFirstVisit.title: Grassic Gibbon Centre, café and St Ternan’s
suggestedFirstVisit.summary: Start at the literary centre and café, then drive or carefully walk the narrow rural lane to the daily-open church and Grassic Gibbon memorial.

dontMiss: St Ternan’s Church and Grassic Gibbon Memorial
townGuide.suggestedTime: 1–3 hours in season; longer only on a house-opening day
townGuide.visitorMood: Focused and rewarding for the right interests, with limited public realm and no independent cluster of shops, streets or all-day activities.
